title: How Representational Priors Shape Generalization in World Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.29168v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World action models (WAMs) are shown to substantially diverge under generalization performance based on their generative backbones. We investigate this gap through the representational geometry that WAMs inherit from their backbones and how policy training reorganizes it. Our central hypothesis is that a useful representational prior would structure geometry that separates nuisance information from the in-distribution manifold in advance of training as a policy. We quantify this with nuisance orthogonality; orthogonality of the feature under visual variation outside the empirical in-distribution manifold. Across various image and video backbones, we show that a higher orthogonality from the representational prior is associated with stronger robustness to visual variations after WAM training, enabling policy generalization measurable prospectively for world models. translated_title: 表征先验如何塑造世界动作模型的泛化能力
translated_abstract: 世界动作模型在泛化性能上因其生成式骨干网络的不同而表现出显著差异。我们通过研究世界动作模型从其骨干网络继承的表征几何结构，以及策略训练如何重组这一结构，来探究这一差距。我们的核心假设是：有用的表征先验会在策略训练之前就构建出一种几何结构，将干扰信息与分布内流形分离开来。我们用“干扰正交性”来量化这一点，即在经验分布内流形之外，特征在视觉变化下的正交性。在多种图像和视频骨干网络上，我们证明表征先验带来的更高正交性与世界动作模型训练后对视觉变化的更强鲁棒性相关，从而使世界模型的策略泛化能力能够被前瞻性地测量。此外，对由此产生的鲁棒世界动作模型的分析揭示了干扰抑制（原文此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出“干扰正交性”这一可前瞻测量的指标，证明世界动作模型的表征先验若能预先将干扰信息与分布内流形分离，则可预测策略训练后对视觉变化的泛化鲁棒性。
